question: Kullu Dussehra is a colourful festival majorly celebrated in which state/union territory?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Kullu Dussehra is a colourful festival that is majorly celebrated in the state of Himachal Pradesh, India.**
 
• The festival is celebrated in the** Kullu Valley,** which lies in the** northern part of Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• It usually takes place in the month of October and is a 7-day long celebration that culminates on the day of** Vijayadashami**, which marks the victory of good over evil.
 
• The festival is known for its **vibrant processions, cultural performances, and the presence of deities **from various temples in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi, being the capital city of India, celebrates a variety of festivals throughout the year.**
 
• Some of the famous festivals celebrated in Delhi are:
 
 
• **Diwali **- It is the festival of lights and is celebrated with great enthusiasm and zeal in India. People decorate their homes with diyas and candles, and burst firecrackers to celebrate the occasion.
 
• **Holi -** This colorful festival is celebrated with great joy and fervor in Delhi. People play with colors and water, and also relish traditional sweets like gujiya and thandai.
 
• **Durga Puja **- This is a major festival for the Bengali community in Delhi. Elaborate pandals are set up across the city, and people come together to worship Goddess Durga and enjoy cultural programs and food.
 
• **Eid al-Fitr **- This is an important festival for the Muslim community in Delhi. It marks the end of the holy month of Ramadan, and people celebrate by offering prayers, exchanging gifts, and feasting with family and friends.
 
• **Christmas **- Although not a traditional Indian festival, Christmas is widely celebrated in Delhi, especially in areas with a large Christian population. The city is decorated with lights and Christmas trees, and people attend midnight masses and enjoy festive food and drinks.
 
 
 
• **One of the most famous festivals of Telangana is Bonalu**.
 
 
• It is celebrated mainly in **Hyderabad, Secunderabad**, and other parts of the state during the **month of Ashada (July-August)** to honor the **goddess Mahankali**.
 
• During Bonalu, devotees offer special** prayers and offerings to the goddess,** which includes rice cooked in a brass or **earthen pot, decorated with turmeric and vermilion.**
 
• Women carry the pots on their heads and take them to the temple, accompanied by drummers and dancers.
 
• The festival is celebrated with great enthusiasm and is an important part of the cultural heritage of **Telangana**.
 
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh is a state in northern India, which is known for its rich cultural heritage and diverse festivals.**
 
• Here are some of the famous festivals celebrated in Uttar Pradesh:
 
 
• **Kumbh Mela**: Kumbh Mela is one of the largest religious gatherings in the world, which takes place every 12 years in Allahabad, Haridwar, Nashik, and Ujjain. It is a Hindu pilgrimage festival where millions of people take a dip in the holy river to wash off their sins.
 
• **Holi**: Holi is a popular festival celebrated in Uttar Pradesh and other parts of India. It is also known as the festival of colors and signifies the victory of good over evil. People celebrate this festival by throwing colored powder, dancing, and feasting.
 
• **Diwali**: Diwali is a festival of lights celebrated all over India, including Uttar Pradesh. It marks the victory of light over darkness and is celebrated by lighting diyas (earthen lamps), bursting fireworks, and exchanging sweets.
 
• **Eid-ul-Fitr**: Eid-ul-Fitr is a Muslim festival celebrated after the holy month of Ramadan. People celebrate this festival by praying, visiting relatives and friends, and exchanging gifts.
 
• **Ram Navami:** Ram Navami is a Hindu festival celebrated to mark the birth of Lord Rama, one of the most revered deities in Hinduism. People celebrate this festival by fasting, praying, and organizing processions.These are just a few of the many festivals celebrated in Uttar Pradesh. The state has a rich cultural heritage, and its festivals reflect the diversity and unity of its people.
